requirement: Reject a duplicate email
scenario: Concurrent signups for the same email
rationale: Verifying a true race between two simultaneous requests needs client-side parallelism this pipeline's sequential Postman/Newman run doesn't provide. The non-concurrent duplicate-rejection scenario for this requirement is covered (see assertions/user-signup.json).

requirement: Reject a duplicate username
scenario: Concurrent signups for the same username
rationale: Same client-side-parallelism blocker as "Reject a duplicate email" - see that entry. The non-concurrent duplicate-username scenario is covered.

requirement: Store the password unrecoverably
scenario: Password is hashed, not stored as plain text
rationale: Verifying the stored credential is a one-way hash (and that the original password verifies against it) needs database/model inspection, not something an HTTP client can observe. "Never return the password" (covered) verifies the HTTP-observable half of this requirement.

requirement: Reject signin for an embargoed account
rationale: Both of this requirement's scenarios need a country's blocked status to change *after* the account already exists (blocked, then a signin attempt; or blocked-then-unblocked, then a signin attempt). Changing the blocked-countries list has no HTTP endpoint - it's admin/database-only - so this pipeline cannot mutate it between requests to set up either scenario.

requirement: Maintain a configurable list of blocked countries
rationale: `embargo` has no endpoint of its own - its check is called internally from signup/signin, not exposed as a route (see sdd_django_demo/embargo/rules.py), so it never appears in the OpenAPI schema this pipeline derives coverage from. The "listed country is blocked" half is exercised indirectly by user-signup's "Reject a submission from a blocked country" assertion; the "unlisted country is allowed" half is exercised indirectly by every other signup assertion, which all submit an unblocked country.

requirement: Match a country case-insensitively
rationale: Same no-endpoint blocker as "Maintain a configurable list of blocked countries" - not independently exercised through signup/signin's exposed fields either, since the blocked-country probe this pipeline sends uses one fixed casing.

requirement: Evaluate checks against the list's current state
rationale: Same no-endpoint blocker as "Maintain a configurable list of blocked countries". Verifying a check reflects a list change made after signup also needs an admin/database mutation between two requests, which this pipeline doesn't perform.

requirement: Deliver a reset code to a registered address
rationale: Verifying mail delivery needs access to the outbound message the app's email backend sends, which isn't exposed over HTTP. "Answer every reset request identically" (covered) verifies the HTTP-observable caller-facing half of this guarantee.

requirement: Deliver the reset link as an absolute address
rationale: Same mail-inspection blocker as "Deliver a reset code to a registered address".

requirement: Deliver nothing to an unregistered address
rationale: Same mail-inspection blocker as "Deliver a reset code to a registered address".

requirement: Leave earlier codes usable when delivery fails
rationale: Needs a simulated mail-delivery failure plus the ability to test the earlier code's usability, which in turn needs a real code obtained from a delivered message (see "Deliver a reset code...").

requirement: A flood cannot leave an address with no usable code
scenario: A flood cannot leave an address with no usable code
rationale: Confirming "the most recently delivered code is still usable" needs a real code obtained from a delivered message, which this pipeline cannot inspect (see "Deliver a reset code..."). The rate-limit mechanics themselves (fixed 429, no retry-time leak) are covered.

requirement: Reaching the limit does not reveal whether an account exists
rationale: Would require repeating the multi-request rate-limit flood for both a registered and an unregistered address and comparing the final refusals - not implemented in this pass to keep the pipeline's runtime bounded; the underlying fixed-body 429 contract is covered by "Limit how often a reset may be requested for one address".

requirement: Serve a page at the delivered link
rationale: This page is served by a plain Django `View`, not a DRF view (see `sdd_django_demo/api/views.py::PasswordResetPageView`), so it is deliberately excluded from the OpenAPI schema drf-spectacular produces. This pipeline's coverage is derived strictly from that schema, so it structurally cannot include a non-DRF page. Covered instead by `sdd_django_demo/api/test_password_reset.py` (pytest).

requirement: Require the two password entries to match
rationale: Same no-DRF-endpoint blocker as "Serve a page at the delivered link" - the two-entry confirmation form only exists on the plain Django page, not the API.

requirement: Report a mismatch before judging the password
rationale: Same no-DRF-endpoint blocker as "Require the two password entries to match".

requirement: Decide the link before the password
rationale: Same no-DRF-endpoint blocker as "Require the two password entries to match".

requirement: Never retain the confirmation entry
rationale: Same no-DRF-endpoint blocker as "Require the two password entries to match".

requirement: Complete a reset through the API with a single password
rationale: This one IS about the DRF confirm endpoint, and every request this pipeline sends it already omits a confirmation field without being rejected for it - but confirming the scenario's full claim ("the request succeeds") needs a real, unexpired reset code, which needs the mail-inspection this pipeline cannot do (see "Deliver a reset code..."/"Accept a reset completion").

requirement: Accept a reset completion
rationale: Only reachable with a genuine, unexpired reset code, which requires the mail-inspection this pipeline cannot do (see "Deliver a reset code..."). The two rejection scenarios for missing fields are covered without a real code.

requirement: Complete a reset with a valid code
rationale: Needs a real, unexpired reset code - see "Accept a reset completion".

requirement: Hold a new password to the signup strength rules
rationale: Needs a real reset code to reach password-strength validation on the completion endpoint - see "Accept a reset completion".

requirement: Expire a reset code after 30 minutes
rationale: Needs a real code and a 30-minute wait, which is impractical for a CI run triggered on every push. Left for manual/long-running verification.

requirement: Retire a reset code once it is used
rationale: Needs a real reset code used once already - see "Accept a reset completion".

requirement: Supersede an earlier unused code
rationale: Needs two real reset codes for the same address to compare - see "Accept a reset completion".

requirement: Reject every bad code identically
scenario: Used and superseded codes are indistinguishable
rationale: The unrecognised-code case is covered without a real code; the expired/used/superseded cases need one - see "Accept a reset completion".

requirement: Invalidate existing authentication tokens on reset
rationale: Needs a completed reset (a real code), which needs the mail-inspection this pipeline cannot do - see "Accept a reset completion".

requirement: Store a new password unrecoverably
rationale: Same database/model-inspection blocker as user-signup's "Store the password unrecoverably".
